book_context: The book is a chronological sequence of failed 'educations'. Each chapter is named for a place or theme, opens a new attempt, and ends by tallying how little was gained. Recurring mechanisms run across chapters: 'accidental education' versus planned study; the eighteenth-century boy facing modern forces; the steps of Ara Coeli as a site of unanswered historical questions; Garibaldi as the 'complexity of simplicity'; the maxim that a friend in power is a friend lost; the habit of holding one's tongue and silence; the woman as a guiding force; and the forward reach to dynamos, force and multiplicity in the late chapters. The selected chapters (V–VIII) move from Berlin's failed Civil Law, through European tourism and Rome, to the Washington secession winter, and then to the London Legation under hostile British recognition of the Confederacy.
continuity_checks: Sumner's denunciation is private, and Henry 'never admitted the rupture'.
Lincoln arrived February 23 and was inaugurated March 4; Henry's task ends when Hay's begins.
The Lincoln misjudgment remains the young man's view, framed by the 'would have lost' admission.
Return to Boston in mid-March, to Horace Gray's office.

essential: The return to Quincy: the father does not mock the Pandects but makes Henry private secretary for the Washington winter; the Wide-Awake torch procession whose air 'was not that of innocence'.
No one wanted or planned the Civil War.
Washington unchanged, a rude colony with little to secede from; the Union only a sentiment.
Everyone as ignorant as he (Sumner's Oxenstiern quote may be compressed). Southern planters as unbalanced and provincial: 'excess of power... held by inadequate hands'.
The North offers only one's own New England type, poised to a fault; Raymond named as a man of the world.
Hope narrows to Sumner and Seward. Sumner: dogmatism of the station, but warranted. The two senators' mutual antipathy, with the naive secretary courting both.

Seward portrait: macaw head and cigar; mask versus features indistinguishable; 'Henry Adams thought it charming'; the effect of unselfishness. Seward and C. F. Adams essentially alike; the Adamses subordinate local to national interests.
Strategy hinges on Virginia; concessions risk dividing the party; Seward's dinner remark.
Secretaries learn nothing; John Hay appears, recognized as a friend; Henry's secret correspondence and ballrooms yield nothing.
Winfield Scott is the only figure equal to the crisis; Lincoln seen once at the Inaugural Ball and judged as lacking force, a judgment flagged as one he 'would have lost' on.
Sumner privately denounces Mr. Adams and breaks with the family; the shock 'opened a chasm'; rebel defections, even Lee's, cost no pang, but Sumner's struck home.
Washington in March 1861: vultures of patronage, a cost of a million lives; return to Horace Gray's law office, 'education in treason' failed.
optional: 'John Adams was better off in Philadelphia' line.
Central and Western names (Preston King, Davis, Lovejoy) and average Congressman/Senator remarks.
Hildreth's hereditary treachery charge (keep the general point).
risks: Para 21 'Friends are born, not made' could be cut for space but is useful; watch the verbatim budget.

voice_profile: Retrospective third-person self-portrait ('Henry Adams', 'the young man', 'one', 'the private secretary') written by an old man about his younger self. The tone is dry irony and steady self-deprecation, and 'education' works as a running ledger that nearly always comes out negative. Characteristic sentence moves include aphoristic reversals ('His first lecture was his last'), paradox and chiasmus, and cumulative semicolon catalogues. Double hyphens mark asides and self-corrections. Adams makes deliberate anachronistic leaps of forty or fifty years and uses mock-scientific or economic vocabulary (equivalents, energy, dynamo, mathematics) for human experience. Animal and martyr images belittle the self (mosquito, cabin-boy, Christian martyrs). The young man's beliefs at the time are kept distinct from the old man's later judgments.
